# New Feature: Tribal Boundaries in climakitae

We're excited to announce that [`climakitae`](https://github.com/cal-adapt/climakitae) now includes tribal and Indigenous territorial boundaries as an available data layer for your climate analysis.

## What's New

You can now visualize and analyze climate data within the geographic context of tribal lands and territories. This feature enables:

- Better geographic context for climate adaptation planning relevant to tribal communities
- Enhanced analysis by overlaying climate projections with tribal boundaries
- Improved community engagement by centering tribal lands in climate assessment workflows

## Data Source

Tribal boundary data is sourced from the [U.S. Department of Interior Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) GeoSpatial Data Repository](https://biamaps.geoplatform.gov/), the official federal source for recognized tribal territorial information.

## How to Use

The tribal boundaries layer can be toggled on and off like any other geographic reference layer in `climakitae`. Simply select the layer from the available boundary options to display tribal territories on your map.

## Important Considerations

While this data provides valuable geographic reference information, we encourage users to:

- Consult directly with tribal nations for decision-making that affects their territories
- Recognize that map data represents one source of information about tribal interests and governance
- Understand that representation varies, with some communities having greater institutional capacity to engage with climate planning processes
- Verify specific boundary information with official tribal documentation when needed for important decisions

Please see our full guidance on [external data boundaries](https://analytics.cal-adapt.org/about/our-project.html) for more information on how to responsibly use this layer in your analysis.

**Have feedback or questions about this feature?** We'd love to hear from you. Please contact us or open an issue on our [GitHub repository](https://github.com/cal-adapt/climakitae/issues).
